# Liquid viscosity from the Pedersen (PFCT) heavy-oil correlation

`eos.viscosity`

## Source

**NeqSim master `PFCTViscosityMethodHeavyOil`**

`calcViscosity` and `getRefComponentViscosity`, ported verbatim

DOI: [10.1016/0009-2509(84)87009-8](https://doi.org/10.1016/0009-2509(84)87009-8)


## What this model is

A **direct** model: a computation over vectors, with no iteration and therefore no algorithm block. It is here because a calculation's inputs are scalars, so a composition vector has nowhere in the calc registry to go - and it is a model rather than a library function so that it goes through the spec-driven pipeline like everything else.

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `components` | - | the substances the mixture is made of, by name, resolved against the component databank with the keycard's overrides applied |
| `T` | K | absolute temperature of the state |
| `P` | Pa | absolute pressure of the state |
| `z` | dimensionless | the mixture's mole fractions, checked rather than renormalised |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `mu` | Pa*s | the liquid dynamic viscosity |

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `T > 0` | raises | an absolute temperature; zero and below are not states |
| `P > 0` | raises | an absolute pressure; zero and below are not states |

## Assumptions

- the correlation is NeqSim's liquid default (`PFCTViscosityMethodHeavyOil`): a methane SRK reference flash, a Tc/Pc/molar-mass mixing rule, the reference-viscosity correlation and a corresponding-states scaling.
- the reference is pure methane solved with the SRK equation of state; the mixture's own cubic and alpha are not consulted.
- a component's `Tc`, `Pc`, `omega`, every `kij` and its molar mass come from the databank with the keycard's overrides applied; a card-added component without a molar mass is refused.
- the four corresponding-states correction factors are their defaults (1.0).
- this is a liquid-phase correlation; it is not the gas viscosity (`eos.chung_viscosity` / `eos.wilke_viscosity`).

## Cases

| Case | Inputs | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `n_butane_at_250_k_and_1_bar` | components = ['n-butane'], T = 250.0, P = 100000.0, z = [1.0] | mu = 0.00027260541411752915 |
